lines: Stereo distortion modelled on pedal circuits the maker built, with a choice of distortion circuit, a choice of tone circuit and a dry/wet blend
Sets the level of distortion, from a little bite at low settings to full destruction at the maximum
Sets the balance between the frequencies, and what it does depends on the tone circuit in use
Sets the balance between the original signal and the distorted one
Attenuates and inverts the FUEL input before it is added to the FUEL knob
Attenuates and inverts the TONE input before it is added to the TONE knob
Attenuates and inverts the BLEND input before it is added to the BLEND knob
Selects the distortion circuit, which the screen names: RODENT, CYLINDER, BLUR, BLUR2, BITE or FEVER
Selects the tone circuit, which the screen names: CREM, DIEZ, PUFF or HIGH
Selects the gain setting, which the screen names
Steps to the next distortion circuit, from RODENT through CYLINDER, BLUR, BLUR2, BITE and FEVER
Steps to the next tone circuit, from CREM through DIEZ, PUFF and HIGH
Steps to the next gain setting
The left channel of the audio input, and with only one input patched the processed signal is sent to both outputs
The right channel of the audio input, and with only one input patched the processed signal is sent to both outputs
A control voltage added to the FUEL setting, scaled by the FUEL attenuverter
A control voltage added to the TONE setting, scaled by the TONE attenuverter
A control voltage added to the BLEND setting, scaled by the BLEND attenuverter
The left channel of the processed signal
The right channel of the processed signal
Flame.notes: The manual documents three distortion circuits (Rodent, Cylinder, Blur) and three tone circuits (Crem, Diez, Puff); the installed 2.0.16 binary carries six and four, listed in strings as RODENT, CYLINDER, BLUR, BLUR2, BITE, FEVER and CREM, DIEZ, PUFF, HIGH. No source says what the GAIN setting does, so its two lines say only that it is stepped and shown on the screen. Parameters 6, 7 and 8 hold the three current settings and have positions at the lower edge of the screen; parameters 9, 10 and 11 are the three buttons under it, confirmed against the rendered panel.

lines: Filter on the CMOS design, which uses a digital inverter chip in place of operational amplifiers, giving a distorted and aggressive character, with lowpass, bandpass, highpass and notch outputs
Sets the frequency at which the filter starts to act: fully counter-clockwise it is closed, fully clockwise it is open
Boosts the frequencies near the cutoff, and this filter does not self-oscillate
Sets how much signal enters the filter, and raising it saturates the filter and adds harmonics
Distorts the output of the filter, which returns harmonics the filter has taken out
Attenuates and inverts the CUT input before it is added to the cutoff, and a 1V/octave signal through it makes the cutoff track pitch
Attenuates and inverts the RES input before it is added to the resonance
Attenuates and inverts the DRIVE input before it is added to the drive
Attenuates and inverts the bite modulation input before it is added to the BITE knob
The audio input to the filter
A control voltage added to the cutoff, scaled by the CUT attenuverter, and tracking 1V per octave when that attenuverter is set for it
A control voltage added to the resonance, scaled by the RES attenuverter
A control voltage added to the drive, scaled by the DRIVE attenuverter
A control voltage added to the bite, scaled by the bite attenuverter
The lowpass output
The bandpass output
The highpass output
The notch output
Ferox.notes: Parameter 8 has no name and no position on the panel and was left out. The bite attenuverter and the bite input carry no printed label of their own on the panel.

lines: A power supply, written by the maker as a joke and given to the people who donated: it provides fixed and variable voltages, and no module in Rack needs a power supply
Sets the voltage at the VAR output, -12V to 12V
A constant voltage set by the knob, anywhere from -12V to 12V
A constant 5V
A constant 12V
A constant -12V
A constant 0V
HyperPower.notes: The jacks run VAR, +5V, +12V, GND, -12V down the panel, so output 4 is above output 3; the tags follow the positions rather than the numbering.

lines: Digital oscillator and LFO on frequency and phase modulation, with a phase section, a noise and tone mix, a chaos section driven by the gate, glide, and a modulation router with six slots
Picks whether the module runs at audio rate as an oscillator or at low frequency as an LFO
Sets the range of the TUNE knob: FINE is a semitone up and down, COARSE is an octave up and down, SEMI is an octave up and down quantized to semitones
Offsets the V/OCT input over the range set by the tune mode switch
Offsets the V/OCT input three octaves up and down, and modulating it produces arpeggios
Sets the balance of even and odd harmonics in the main oscillator: fully counter-clockwise gives a square, fully clockwise a saw
Sets the number of harmonics in the main oscillator, from the bare fundamental to the full wave, much like a lowpass filter
Sets the level of white noise added to the mix, which suits percussive sounds
Sets the frequency of the FM modulator, over the range set by the RATIO and FREE switch
Sets how much the modulator frequency-modulates the main oscillator
Applies a fold-like distortion to the phase of the main oscillator, which sounds like overtones added to the tone
Transforms the phase of the main oscillator in a logarithmic or exponential way, for a thinner or fatter sound
Changes the amplitude of the phase of the main oscillator, which sounds like hard clipping
Adds positive feedback to the phase of the main oscillator, for a resonating sound
Sets how far the parameters can move when a gate arrives, and at the maximum they can move from minimum to maximum
Sets how long the parameters stay away from their set values after a gate: a low setting snaps back for percussive sounds, and at the maximum they stay put until the next gate sets a new random state
Picks how the modulator frequency is chosen: RATIO restricts it to factors of the main frequency, from a half to eight times it, and FREE allows any frequency in that range
Sets how much the signal at the FM input frequency-modulates the main oscillator
Sets the maximum rate at which the pitch follows a change of the V/OCT input
SKIPGATE leaves the glide out when the pitch changes at the same moment as the gate, ALWAYS applies the glide to every pitch change
Picks the wave of the modulator: SAW for an edgier result, SINE for softer modulation
Balances the sound of the oscillator: counter-clockwise the highs are removed and the lows enhanced
Attenuates and inverts the modulation input of the same number before it reaches the control assigned to that slot
Assigns that modulation slot: press it, then move the control the slot should change
Sets the pitch, 1V per octave, where 0V is a C1
A gate that drives the chaos section, and whose timing the SKIPGATE glide mode uses
An external signal that frequency-modulates the main oscillator, scaled by the EXT.FM knob
A control voltage for the control assigned to the modulation slot of the same number
The mixed waves and noise
Noxious.notes: Parameter 6 has no name and no position on the panel and was left out. The monophonic model declares the polyphonic section's parameters, inputs and outputs but gives none of them a position, so none of them is tagged.

Noxious-Poly.notes: In each extra voice the pitch jack is above the gate jack, while the indices run gate first: input 9 is the gate of voice A and input 10 its pitch. Parameter 6 has no name and no position on the panel and was left out.

lines: Dual low pass gate on a modified version of the best known Buchla design, with a detailed vactrol model, switchable VCA action, and a left and a right channel that also work as a stereo filter
Sets the frequency at which both filters start to act: fully counter-clockwise they are closed, fully clockwise they are open
Boosts the frequencies near the cutoff in both filters, and past a point they self-oscillate and can be played as a sound source
Sets how much signal enters both filters, and raising it saturates them and adds harmonics
Attenuates and inverts the CV input before it is added to the cutoff, and a 1V/octave signal through it makes the cutoff track pitch
Attenuates and inverts the RES input before it is added to the resonance
Attenuates and inverts the DRIVE input before it is added to the drive
Attenuates or amplifies the gate signal on that side before it reaches the cutoff, and the amplification lets a low gate signal open the filter further
ON puts the vactrol model in the gate path, which gives smoother transitions from its memory effect; OFF lets the gate signal change the cutoff at once
ON makes the gate change the amplitude of the signal as well as the cutoff, which greatly reduces the resonance; OFF leaves the gate acting on the cutoff alone
LINK has both gate signals control both filters, UNLINK has the left gate control the left filter and the right gate the right filter
The left channel of the audio input
The right channel of the audio input
A signal that opens and closes the filters, scaled by its own GATE attenuverter, reaching one filter or both according to the GATES switch
A control voltage added to the resonance, scaled by the RES attenuverter
A control voltage added to the drive, scaled by the DRIVE attenuverter
A control voltage added to the cutoff, scaled by the CV attenuverter, and tracking 1V per octave when that attenuverter is set for it
The left channel of the processed signal
The right channel of the processed signal
Comb filter with high feedback and input distortion for metallic and glitchy sounds, playable as a Karplus-Strong generator through its V/OCT input, with an LFO of its own
Sets the spacing of the frequency combs, which is the main sonic character of the filter
Sets how much of the output is circulated back to the input, which sets the decay when the filter is fed short pulses, and at high settings makes it self-oscillate
Sets the level of the input signal, and a high setting saturates the filter and distorts the sound
Attenuates and inverts the CV input before it is added to the FREQUENCY knob
Attenuates and inverts the FEEDBACK input before it is added to the FEEDBACK knob
Attenuates and inverts the DRIVE input before it is added to the DRIVE knob
Sets how much of the LFO is sent to the frequency
Sets how much of the LFO is sent to the feedback
Sets the LFO frequency, from very slow to audio rate
Picks the comb filter, Comb+ or Comb-, one of which enhances the low frequencies and the other the highs, depending on the input sound
Picks the LFO wave: TRI for a triangle, SAW for a saw, CHAOS for a chaotic wave
A control voltage added to the feedback, scaled by the FEEDBACK attenuverter
A control voltage added to the drive, scaled by the DRIVE attenuverter
Sets the frequency of the filter, 1V per octave, offset by the FREQUENCY knob
A control voltage added to the frequency, scaled by the CV attenuverter
A trigger that resets the LFO to its initial state
The left channel of the audio input
The right channel of the audio input
The left channel of the processed signal
The right channel of the processed signal
The LFO signal, which is unipolar
Rescomb2.notes: Parameter 9 has no name and no position on the panel and was left out. The manual does not say whether the CV input beside the FREQUENCY knob tracks 1V per octave, and the module has a separate V/OCT jack that does, so the CV input is coloured cv.

lines: Filter modelled in detail on a famous Russian circuit, with a lowpass and a bandpass output and enough resonance to self-oscillate
Sets the frequency at which the filter starts to act: fully counter-clockwise it is closed, fully clockwise it is open
Boosts the frequencies near the cutoff, and past a point the filter self-oscillates and can be played as a sound source
Sets how much signal enters the filter, and raising it saturates the filter and adds harmonics
Attenuates and inverts the CUTOFF input before it is added to the cutoff, and a 1V/octave signal through it makes the cutoff track pitch
Attenuates and inverts the RESONANCE input before it is added to the resonance
Attenuates and inverts the DRIVE input before it is added to the drive
The audio input, which can be left unpatched and the filter played by raising the resonance until it self-oscillates
A control voltage added to the cutoff, scaled by the CUTOFF attenuverter, and tracking 1V per octave when that attenuverter is set for it
A control voltage added to the resonance, scaled by the RESONANCE attenuverter
A control voltage added to the drive, scaled by the DRIVE attenuverter
The lowpass output
The bandpass output
Vortex.notes: Parameter 6 is a two-position switch printed LV and RS on the panel; the maker's tooltip names it Model, and nothing in the manual, the panel or the binary's strings says what the two settings are, so it has no line.
